existing_localTerm:
The Constitution's own term is Indigenous peoples, in art 149G
The Amerindian Act 2006 says Amerindian, including for the languages themselves
The education strategic plan calls the same communities indigenous
existing_standing:
Constitution art 149G gives indigenous peoples a right to protect and preserve their languages
It runs with cultural heritage and way of life, in one article of the fundamental rights title
Amerindian Act 2006 s41 makes promoting recognition and use a National Toshaos Council function
existing_mediumOfInstruction:
The ministry supports mother-tongue use where possible in the early years of school
It reaches indigenous communities where English may not be the first language
UNESCO's PEER profile records limited attempts, so this is practice rather than entitlement
existing_taughtAsSubject: Nothing timetabled is recorded, only support for projects such as the Macushi Language project

Kroon, S. & Yağmur, K., Meertaligheid in het onderwijs in Suriname (2012), commissioned by the Surinamese ministry of education and the Nederlandse Taalunie
Meertaligheid in het onderwijs in Suriname – publication record, Nederlandse Taalunie
Grondwet van de Republiek Suriname (S.B. 1987 no.116), art. 8

existing_localTerm:
Inheemse en marron gemeenschappen is the term in the 2024-2031 national education plan
Meertaligheid is the policy heading, one of eight areas given a position paper
A ministry-commissioned study groups them as inheemse, geimporteerde and ontstane talen
existing_standing:
Dutch has been the official language since 1667, in a ministry-commissioned study
Constitution art 8 bars discrimination on grounds of language, among other statuses
That study records state policy as never having been aimed at multilingualism
existing_mediumOfInstruction:
Classroom findings come from a study of pupils' and teachers' practices and views
Dutch is the official language and the central language of instruction
Home languages are used in class incidentally and not systematically, teachers report
Teachers hold that pupils are in principle not allowed to use other languages in class
existing_taughtAsSubject:
Offering Suriname's languages as a school subject is put as a question for policy
Pupils named their own and others' home languages among those they would like to learn
The 2024-2031 plan folds meertaligheid into curriculum renewal at primary level

existing_localTerm:
English Creole is the curriculum's term for the language children bring to school
Spanish, Hindi, Creole and French Patois also spoken alongside English
Awareness of the two systems is built into the primary ELA programme
Curriculum works to minimise the perception of bad English use or broken English
existing_standing:
Draft Education Policy Paper 2017-22 promises equal access regardless of language and ethnicity
The plan mentions multilingual education but carries no specific policies on it
existing_mediumOfInstruction:
Standard English is the target language; English Creole is the first language pupils bring
Creole is a natural support when communication breaks down teaching Standard English
Class discussion at primary uses both Creole English and Standard English
existing_taughtAsSubject:
Taught about inside the National Primary English Language Arts curriculum
Contrastive analysis between English Creole and Standard English is curriculum content
Pupils distinguish the two by phonology, morphology and syntax
Goal is code switching between Standard English and English Creole

docLinks.label: UNESCO GEM Report PEER, Antigua and Barbuda country profile, INCLUSION (section 3 Laws, Plans, Policies and Programmes, incl. Ethnic and linguistic groups and Migrants)

Antigua and Barbuda, The Education Act, 2008 (No. 21 of 2008), s.3(3)(g) and s.3(4), published in the Official Gazette Vol. XXIX No. 10 — copy hosted on theiguides.org, as laws.gov.ag would not answer

existing_localTerm: The 2013 special education needs policy speaks of the form of language in the home
existing_standing: Not established from the sources consulted. The Education Act 2008 names language only among what schooling must promote understanding of, and PEER's linguistic and ethnic groups section is about special educational needs rather than any standing.
existing_mediumOfInstruction: Not established from the sources consulted. The Education Act 2008 carries no medium-of-instruction provision, and PEER treats a home language different from the language of teaching as a care point in assessment, not as a medium.
existing_taughtAsSubject:
Education Act goal: understanding the history, language and culture of Antigua and Barbuda
Minister promotes the goal through basic and continuing education strategies

Secretaría de Educación de Honduras, Sub-Dirección General de Educación para Pueblos Indígenas y Afrohondureños (SDGEPIAH): historia, lineamientos pedagógicos y fundamentación de la EIB

existing_localTerm:
Educacion Intercultural Bilingue, EIB, is the term, for pueblos autoctonos y afro antillanos
Word order marks two approaches: Bilingue Intercultural where the mother tongue is strong
Intercultural Bilingue is the term where those languages have fallen into disuse
The unit is the Subdireccion General de Educacion para Pueblos Indigenas y Afrohondurenos
existing_standing:
Constitution art 173 obliges the State to preserve and stimulate the native cultures
The programme was legalised by acuerdo presidencial 0719 on 3 August 1994
EIB was then created as a modality of the education system by the Secretaria de Educacion
UNESCO PEER records the State as responsible for regulating intercultural bilingual education
existing_mediumOfInstruction:
Cognitive development is done in the first language, inside its own grammatical structure
That track covers the miskito, Tawahka, garifuna and English-speaking peoples
For Pesh, Nahua, Tolupan, Chorti and Lenca, literacy and cognition are in Spanish
Where children arrive without the indigenous language, the mother tongue is taken as Spanish
existing_taughtAsSubject:
In that second group the indigenous languages are handled as second languages
The second language is learned for communication and for specific areas of universal knowledge
For Lenca no native speakers have been found, only glossaries and short phrases
The stated aim is an additive bilingualism with interculturality

existing_standing: Constitution article 2 makes Spanish the official language of the Republic
existing_mediumOfInstruction: Not established from the sources consulted. Article 2 of the 2019 Constitution makes Spanish the official language and names no other, carrying no medium-of-instruction provision, and PEER publishes no Inclusion chapter for Cuba at all.
existing_taughtAsSubject: Not established from the sources consulted. The 2019 Constitution names no language but Spanish and no language subject, and PEER publishes no Inclusion chapter for Cuba against which that could be checked.

docLinks.label: Ministry of Education, St. Kitts and Nevis, Language Policy, 3 June 2018

existing_localTerm:
The Language Policy calls it the dialect, used in schools in informal discourse
Also named Creole-Influenced varieties, abbreviated CIV in the policy
Curriculum document says several varieties exist and there is no standard form
Educators accept the English-based dialect as a legitimate first language
existing_standing:
English is the official language and the one used for instruction and examinations
Ministry of Education supports a language awareness approach as national language policy
Stated aim is that all students appreciate the Federation's culture and its dialect
existing_mediumOfInstruction:
Language Awareness is the chosen policy, using both varieties to study contrasts
Teachers accept the child's language and promote interaction in English as second dialect
Songs, poems and stories used in the home dialect alongside Standard English
existing_taughtAsSubject:
Primary School Interim Curriculum Language Arts teaches English as a second language
Contrastive analysis draws attention to differences between the vernacular and the standard
Awareness of contrasts starts with pronunciation, structural points in higher grades
Approach aims to let students read the first language and write in it creatively
